item.title: Deferred Voxel Shading for Real Time Global Illumination
item.description: Computing indirect illumination is a challenging and complex problem for real-time rendering in 3D applications. This global illumination approach computes indirect lighting in real time utilizing a simplified version of the outgoing radiance and the scene stored in voxels.

item.title: Simple Multi-texture Terrain Rendering
item.description: Terrain rendering from heightmaps generated with libnoise, started as a college assignment. It is textured by height, lit through the day by path-traced lightmaps, and drawn with geomipmapping.

item.title: Volume Rendering with Style Transfer Function
item.description: An interactive volume renderer where style transfer functions decide how each part of a scan looks. Every density range gets a lit sphere image, a “style”, along with its color and opacity, so bone, skin or leaves each get their own material. The volume lights itself with soft shadows, ambient occlusion and one bounce of indirect light. The technique is based on this paper.

item.title: Stereoscopy
item.description: Stereoscopy is a technique that enables us to create the illusion of depth for binocular vision. You need special lenses to appreciate the effect. In this college project I implemented a basic rendering engine using C++ with stereoscopy.

item.title: Computer Graphics Basic Mapping Techniques
item.description: One of my first computer graphics assignments: a real time scene with shadow mapping, reflections and refractions from cube maps, normal and parallax occlusion mapping, and physically based shading, with object selection and transforms through the UI.

item.title: Simple Raytracer
item.description: This was an extremely simple raytracer I wrote in college for an assignment. Here I could learn a lot about the mathematics and physics that makeup light rendering.
